title: H. G. Wells: The War of the Worlds — Ep 07/27 — "How I Reached Home"
description:
The War of the Worlds, Episode 7. Of the running he keeps nothing — trees, and the shock of hitting them, and the certainty that somewhere above him that blade of heat is still turning. He goes down at last by the wayside near the bridge that crosses the canal by the gasworks, and lies still a long while.

Then he sits up, and the fear comes off him like a garment. His hat is gone and his collar has torn off its stud, and the silent common and the starting flames are already a dream he has just left. He walks unsteadily over the bridge. A workman with a basket wishes him good night and he answers with a noise. A train goes over the Maybury arch, a long caterpillar of lighted windows, and it is gone. All of it ordinary, all of it certain. And two miles back, that.

He stops at a gate where three neighbours stand talking, and asks what news there is from the common. They ask whether he has not just been there. They want to know what everyone is making such a fuss about. He tries to tell them about the men from Mars, and all three of them laugh at him; he finds he cannot say it, and goes on home with the worst news in England still in his mouth.

His wife opens the door and steps back at the look of him. He sits down at a cold dinner he never touches, drinks some wine, and tells her what he has seen — and then spends the evening reassuring her: they are the most sluggish things alive, they may keep the pit but they cannot get out of it. She says, again and again, the one true thing anybody says all evening.

Chapter VII of Book One of H. G. Wells's The War of the Worlds (1898), in the public domain.

— The Keeper's Lantern —
Every episode is one whole chapter, in order, from the first page to the last.
